title: The Neighbours
blurb: House C rebuilds the room from the Well: it wipes its own copy, reads the newest Book and every scroll in order, and refuses to go on past a missing one. Every workerd tick pays for a trip to the Well. Then the lamps change to celld's town, where the owner's neighbours press each page onto their own disks and the bell can ring before the Well has the page. The tail now lives outside the Well: epoch shelves fence it but cannot recover it, so a successor reads the old owner's log record first, fences it, seals and collects the neighbours' notebooks, uploads them and only then restores. At least one neighbour must certify a complete tail; without one, the room stays shut.

shots.setting: the harbour town, canonical night (illustrative): House C's upper window and the square below, the Well and the Plate; moonlight low-left, C's window lamp the warm practical

lines.text: Back to workerd's town, the night A went dark. House C holds the Plate: nine, from seven.
lines.direction: quiet resumption, picking a story up mid-page; a light stress on 'claimed' (we know claimed is not opened)

lines.text: First it throws away its own copy of the room.
lines.direction: plain, a little brisk; housekeeping before the real work

lines.text: It reads the newest Book, then each scroll in order, skipping pages already laid down.
lines.direction: steady, methodical, one clause per step; 'in order' slightly weighted

lines.text: A missing scroll in the middle stops the restore cold.
lines.direction: drop the pace; 'cold' flat and final

lines.text: A checksum can say a scroll is damaged. Never what it said.
lines.direction: dry, a teacher's small smile on 'Never'

lines.text: Pages are laid down again; no code is re-run.
lines.direction: matter-of-fact, the two halves balanced

lines.text: Message forty-two is back. Only then does C send down its own Book, and open the Plate.
lines.direction: a quiet release on 'back'; then exact and deliberate on 'Only then'

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: workerd's restore, step by step (badge 'workerd · 28 Oct' on the wellhead, named on 'workerd's'). Iris opens on House C's window lamp (beat iris). Canonical town at L3, the square at L4; slow crane down from C's upper window to the Well (≤ 4% frame width per second). On 'Plate' push in: the Plate reads C · 9 · from 7, crown lamp UNLIT (illustrative epochs; claimed, not opened). On 'throws' C's keeper tips a small local ledger into a stove; it curls to ash (the non-authoritative local copy). On 'Book' the Well's rope draws up a bound Book tagged 'session 7' onto C's pulley line; on 'scroll' four rolled scrolls follow in order, each knot with a stamped tag; at C's window desk the keeper lays pages into the Room Lantern's book; on 'skipping' one page already laid flashes and is set aside unlaid. On 'missing' a GHOST what-if: the chain of scrolls shows a dark gap between the second and third; the keeper's hands stop; the reading lamp holds (no red; this is a rule, not tonight). On 'checksum' a scroll's cord knot glints and a crumpled scroll rolls out unreadable; on 'Never' its panel stays blank. The ghost dissolves; the true chain is whole. On 'Pages' pages drop into the lantern's book as ink silhouettes, no figures move inside (no code re-run). On 'back' slip #42 glows in the lantern. On 'open' C sends its own small Book down the line; the from tile turns to 9 and the crown lamp lights. Label at upper right, never below y 634.

lines.text: This is celld's town, version 0.6.3. By default, the owner hands each write to one or two neighbours.
lines.spoken: This is celld's town, version zero point six point three. By default, the owner hands each write to one or two neighbours.
lines.direction: a fresh start, a guide arriving in a new town; the version said cleanly

lines.text: Each must press the page onto its own disk before it answers. That press is called fsync.
lines.direction: slow and physical on 'press the page onto its own disk'; then naming the term, lightly

lines.text: When every neighbour in the proof has pressed, the bell can ring before the page reaches the Well. The upload follows.
lines.direction: 'every' weighted; a small turn of surprise on 'before the page reaches the Well'; 'The upload follows' as an afterthought

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: celld's fleet, the first principle. The lamp change completes: the backlight rises in labGreen; the same terrace (geography lock), the wellhead now carries the brass badge 'celld 0.6.3' (named on 'celld's'), and celld's Plate above it is a plain plate with no candle scale (no workerd lease numbers anywhere). House A's lamp is the owner; in the upper windows of Houses B and C two copyists sit at desks, each with a notebook and a small iron book press (copyist-1 in B, copyist-2 in C). Slow truck right from A to B (≤ 5% width/s). On 'hands' A's keeper sends one committed page along two short neighbour lines (new thin cords from A's sill to B's and C's sills, never to the Well): each copyist copies it into the notebook's newest line. On 'press' copyist-1 turns the press screw a full turn and the notebook flattens under the platen; the platen locks with a small brass tab (pressed). On 'fsync' the term tag paints; copyist-2 turns its press the same way. On 'every' both press tabs glow; only when BOTH are locked does A's bell swing (beat bell on 'ring'): the latch on the Room Lantern's door lifts and slip #42's tick lands, while the scroll for that page is still on A's sill, not yet sent. On 'upload' the scroll rolls down A's pulley line into the Well. Hold on the two pressed notebooks. Text sits upper left; bottom 12% clear.

lines.text: Now count. The owner never counts itself.
lines.direction: a teacher at the board; 'never' firm

lines.text: One house alone gets no fleet. It falls back on the Well's proof: much slower, still correct.
lines.direction: a small shrug in 'much slower', reassurance in 'still correct'

lines.text: Two running houses: one neighbour, enough for a proof. Three or more: two neighbours, three copies.
lines.direction: counting on fingers, a beat between the two halves

lines.text: Until a second neighbour joins, a fresh write's proof rests on two copies: the owner's and one neighbour's.
lines.direction: slower; 'two copies' set down carefully, it matters later

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the arithmetic of celld's fleet, shown by lamps (badge 'celld 0.6.3' stays on the wellhead, unnamed here). Occluder wipe behind the L6 lamp-post into a wide two-shot of the terrace; camera locked off, a slight dolly in through the shot. Start with ONLY House A lit; B and C dark. On 'itself' a small ink ring around A's own notebook stays empty: the owner's copy is never a vote. On 'alone' A's page has no neighbour cord to follow; instead its scroll makes the whole slow trip down the pulley line into the Well, and A's bell rings only when the Well's bucket comes up (beat wellproof on 'slower'). On 'Two' House B lights; one neighbour cord strings from A to B; one press turns; the bell rings sooner. On 'Three' House C lights; a second cord; two presses; a row of three small page silhouettes stands on A's, B's and C's sills (three copies). On 'Until' rewind to two lit houses: the fresh page stands certified on two sills, A's and B's, and a thin gold outline joins those two proof copies (beat twoPlaces on 'two'); the Well below is still empty of it.

lines.text: Now replay that night in celld's town: the owner dies while forty-two lives only in the neighbours' notebooks.
lines.direction: low and plain, the stakes named without drama

lines.text: Pull the pin.
lines.direction: the house refrain, quiet, a half-smile

lines.text: In celld's Well, each epoch writes under its own shelf, so a stale owner can only add to an old shelf, never to the new owner's.
lines.direction: explaining the clever part fairly; 'its own shelf' clear

lines.text: That fences the Well. It cannot fetch what only the neighbours hold. Forty-two is gone.
lines.direction: the turn: 'cannot' weighted; 'Forty-two is gone' flat, almost a whisper

lines.text: Or the old owner was only asleep, and wakes to ring one more bell.
lines.direction: dry, the teacher who enjoys a good failure

lines.text: Pin back. Before its first tick from the neighbours, each celld session creates its own log record in the Well.
lines.direction: brisk on 'Pin back', then measured; 'before its first such tick' exact

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the tail outside the Well, and the pin (the neighbours' wax-seal stamp, seated on a hook by B's sill). Lamp change into emberRed. Wide on the terrace: on 'dies' House A's window gutters out; in B's and C's upper windows the two notebooks still hold their newest pressed line (#42's page), and the Well holds nothing of it. On 'Pull' the demonstrator's hand slides in from the lower RIGHT and pulls the red-tagged pin from the wax-seal stamp; the stamp goes slack. Crane down into a cutaway of the Well's side: stone shelves, each carved with an epoch number (illustrative 7 above, 8 below). On 'shelf' a ghost of A's keeper sets a late scroll on shelf 7, while shelf 8, the successor's, stays untouched (beat fence on 'never'). On 'fetch' crane back up: the new owner in C restores only from the Well; the room's book is laid without #42's page, and the slip in the lantern loses its tick (beat gone on 'gone'). On 'asleep' rewind: A's lamp flickers back on (a paused process, not a dead one); A sends its next page; both copyists, unsealed, press it; A's bell rings once more for a room it no longer owns (beat stale on 'bell'). On 'Pin' the hand reseats the pin; the light begins to return to labGreen. On 'record' a small brass record tile is created at the wellhead, only if none exists, its shutter falling after it (beat record). Label upper right; nothing below y 634.

shots.setting: parchment plate: celld's recovery gate, six engraved steps in ink pictograms (the guarantees of 21 October 2026)

lines.text: So a successor reads that record before it reads the Well.
lines.direction: measured; 'before' the hinge of the sentence

lines.text: Absent: the old session never ticked ahead of the Well. Sealed: someone already recovered it.
lines.direction: two crisp cases, a beat between them

lines.text: Open, or still recovering: fence it with a compare and swap. Seal every neighbour it can reach, collect their pages, upload them, and mark the record sealed.
lines.direction: a recipe read out step by step; a small breath after each comma; never rushed

lines.text: Only then restore. With its neighbours sealed, the old owner cannot win another bell.
lines.direction: 'Only then' slow; the second sentence quiet and satisfied

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: THE RECOVERY GATE (badge 'celld 0.6.3' engraved at the plate's top corner). Paper fold from the labGreen terrace into a parchment plate, camera locked, a very slow push. Title engraved at top-left. Down the plate, six numbered stations as ink pictograms (numerals only, no sentences): 1 a brass record tile; 2 the Tooth with a swap card; 3 two notebooks with wax seals; 4 pages gathered into a scroll; 5 the Well; 6 the record tile with a seal on it; and at the far right, behind a closed gate, a bound Book (restore). On 'record' station 1's tile is lifted by an ink hand (the successor's keeper, not the demonstrator). On 'Absent' an empty hook beside it: the gate opens straight to the Book (that session never ticked ahead of the Well). On 'Sealed' the tile shows a seal: the gate opens straight to the Book again. Both short paths fade back. On 'Open' the tile shows an open eye; the long path inks in station by station on the words: 'fence' the Tooth clicks and the tile's notch is re-cut (station 2); 'Seal' red wax stamps across both notebooks (3); 'collect' their pages roll into one scroll (4); 'upload' it drops into the Well (5); 'mark' a seal lands on the record tile (6). On 'restore' the gate swings and the Book opens. The quote fragment sits in a cartouche at the UPPER RIGHT from 'Open' to the end; nothing in the bottom 12%. STAGING NOTE (ch07-s03 to s07): the successor is House C's node; its keeper stands at C's door, not in the open square; C's own notebook is one of the two recovery reads.

lines.text: Now the hard rule. At least one current neighbour must hand over its complete range of retained pages.
lines.direction: firm and clear; 'at least one' and 'complete' carry the weight

lines.text: Two made-up cases. One notebook is water-damaged, but the other is complete: recovery proceeds.
lines.direction: 'made-up' plainly; a lift of relief on 'proceeds'

lines.text: Now one notebook is incomplete, and the other damaged. Nobody can prove the whole tail, so the door stays shut.
lines.direction: slower; 'Nobody can prove' level; 'stays shut' final, not tragic

lines.text: And a neighbour that answers with an error has not proved its pages absent.
lines.direction: quietly exact; 'not proved' stressed

lines.text: The room would rather stay shut than come back missing a promise.
lines.direction: the chapter's line; warm, unhurried, a little proud of the machine

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: A COMPLETE TAIL (badge 'celld 0.6.3' on the wellhead, unnamed). Paper fold back to the terrace; medium two-shot of B's and C's upper windows, the copyists at their desks, both notebooks wax-sealed from the gate. The successor's keeper stands on the square below with a lantern, a scroll case open. Each notebook's spine carries a band that shows its retained range: a full ink band = complete; a band with a missing segment = incomplete; a band blurred and water-stained = damaged. On 'complete' both copyists hold their notebooks to the window. CASE ONE on 'water-damaged': copyist-1's band in B is stained; on 'other' copyist-2's band in C is full and sharp; its pages ride down to the keeper, the gate (seen small at the wellhead) opens, the keeper's lantern brightens (beat proceeds). Ink-bleed rewind. CASE TWO on 'incomplete': copyist-1's band now has a gap; on 'damaged' copyist-2's band blurs; the keeper waits; nothing rides down; on 'shut' the Room Lantern's door stays latched, unlit, and the gate stays closed. On 'error' a variation: copyist-2's window answers the keeper with a crossed slip instead of its notebook; the keeper does NOT strike that notebook off: a small hourglass appears beside it and the keeper keeps asking (it might still hold pages). On 'promise' slow push in on the closed door. Quote cartouche at upper right, label at upper left; bottom 12% clear.

lines.text: Houses that restart together still lend each other their notebooks. Recovery can take minutes; a waiting request gives up only after two hundred and forty tries.
lines.direction: patient, reassuring; 'minutes' with a small shrug

lines.text: In our harbour the notebooks are whole. The lantern relights; forty-two keeps its tick.
lines.direction: a quiet arrival; the tick line soft and pleased

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: patience, and the room returns (badge 'celld 0.6.3', unnamed). Occluder wipe behind the L6 lamp-post to the wide terrace. All three houses flicker dark together, then relight together (a shared restart). On 'lend' notebooks pass between B's and C's windows along the neighbour cords, each house answering the other's seal-and-tail requests before its own recovery is finished. On 'minutes' a slow sand-glass on the wellhead turns over once, then again (retries with a pause between; no numbers shown). On 'whole' both notebook spine bands show full and sharp; the pages ride down to C's keeper; the gate at the wellhead opens. On 'relights' the Room Lantern relights in House C's window; slow push in to the sender's slip #42, whose ink tick is still there (beat tick on 'tick'). Hold on the lantern glow; labGreen eases a touch warmer for the coming ending. No text items; bottom 12% clear.
